found.lens: Mathematical relativity / differential geometry: 3+1 and hypersurface geometry (ADM, GHY, Israel junctions, Brown–York, initial-data/conformal method), boundary-term and variational bookkeeping, curvature normalizations shared with math.DG, spinor-bundle and symplectic conventions, and the string/PM/PN habit of using a "unit-setting" constant as an order-counting grading. Sources checked this round: Gourgoulhon's 3+1 notes (K = −3H in FLRW) vs Wald's K_ab = ∇_a n_b; instanton-number normalization variants; explicit recomputation of the scalar-field stress tensor, the Hamilton-equation sign chain, and the ψχ = −ψ_αχ^α spinor identity.

gaps.name: Extrinsic-curvature sign × normal orientation (the whole hypersurface axis)
gaps.what_breaks: The tool's sign axis covers bulk curvature (Riemann sign, Ricci contraction, ε0123) but has nothing for hypersurface geometry. K_ab is 1/length in every convention, so dimensional analysis is blind, yet its sign is set by TWO independent declarations that papers usually state only one of: (i) K_ab = +∇_a n_b (Wald, Poisson's Toolkit) vs K_ab = −∇_a n_b = −(1/2)£_n γ_ab (MTW, Gourgoulhon, and essentially all numerical relativity), and (ii) which way the unit normal points (outward vs inward for a timelike wall, future- vs past-pointing for a slice). Only the product is observable, so a reader who imports a formula from one paper into another flips the sign of: the GHY boundary term, the Hamiltonian- and momentum-constraint cross terms, the ADM conjugate momentum π^ij ∝ K^ij − γ^ij K, the Israel junction surface stress tensor, the Brown–York quasilocal energy density, and the sign of 'collapse vs expansion' in K.
gaps.magnitude: Overall sign on K_ab and on every quantity linear in it (GHY term, π^ij, S_ab, Brown–York ε). Quantities quadratic in K (the Hamiltonian constraint's K_abK^ab − K², the ADM kinetic term) are invariant, which is exactly why the error survives half of a paper's consistency checks.
gaps.example: FLRW with unit lapse, γ_ij = a²δ_ij: MTW/Gourgoulhon/NR convention K_ij = −(1/2)£_n γ_ij gives K = −3H; Wald's K_ab = ∇_a n_b gives K = +3H. Round 2-sphere of radius r in flat R³ with outward normal: K = +2/r (Wald) vs K = −2/r (MTW). Israel junction: [K_ab] − h_ab[K] = −8πS_ab (Poisson's Toolkit, K = +∇n, normal from '−' side to '+' side) vs [K_ab] − h_ab[K] = +8πS_ab under the flipped K convention or the reversed normal.

If absent, infer from a fiducial identity present in the text: K = ∓3H in FLRW; K = ±2/r for a sphere; whether the paper says a collapsing region has K > 0; whether the total action carries +2∮√h K or −2∮√h K; whether the citation for conventions is MTW/Gourgoulhon/Alcubierre (minus) or Wald/Poisson (plus). Separately grep for the normal declaration ('outward-pointing', 'future-directed', 'pointing from Σ⁻ to Σ⁺'); a paper that declares neither should be flagged as under-determined, not guessed.

gaps.name: Stress tensor from metric variation: sign, index position of the varied metric, and Hilbert-vs-canonical kind
gaps.what_breaks: T_μν is dimensionally identical under all variants, but its sign is fixed by a three-way interlock the tool does not model: the index position of the metric being varied (δ/δg^{μν} vs δ/δg_{μν}, which alone flips the sign since δg^{μν} = −g^{μα}g^{νβ}δg_{αβ}), the explicit sign in front of the 2/√−g, and the sign convention for the matter Lagrangian in S = ∫√−g(R/2κ ± L_m). Get any one wrong and the source term in G_μν = 8πT_μν changes sign — gravity becomes repulsive — with no dimensional symptom. Compounding it, 'T_μν' may denote the Hilbert tensor, the canonical Noether tensor, or the Belinfante-improved one; these differ not by a constant but by improvement terms (for a non-minimally coupled scalar, by 2ξ(g_μν□ − ∇_μ∇_ν)φ²), so the tool cannot repair a mismatch by any multiplicative rider.
gaps.magnitude: Sign flip (attractive ↔ repulsive source). Additional factor-2 fork if a paper defines T via δ(√−g L_m)/δg without the 2. Hilbert-vs-canonical mismatch is a whole extra tensor, not a factor.
gaps.example: Mostly-plus signature, L_m = −(1/2)g^{μν}∂_μφ∂_νφ − V(φ). With T_μν = −(2/√−g) δS_m/δg^{μν} one gets T_μν = ∂_μφ∂_νφ − g_μν[(1/2)(∂φ)² + V], hence T_00 = (1/2)φ̇² + V > 0 (verified by direct variation, using δ√−g/δg^{μν} = −(1/2)√−g g_μν). The same expression written as T_μν = +(2/√−g) δS_m/δg^{μν} — which appears in print — yields a negative energy density. The consistent 'plus' form is the one with the lower-index variation: T^{μν} = +(2/√−g) δS_m/δg_{μν}.
gaps.fingerprint: Parse the definitional equation for the triple (sign, index position of the varied metric, sign of L_m in the action) and check the parity of the product against the paper's signature convention. Independently, run a positivity sanity check on any canonical scalar or perfect fluid appearing in the paper: if the paper's own conventions give ρ = T_μν u^μ u^ν < 0 for a minimally coupled scalar, the declaration is internally inconsistent. Detect Hilbert vs canonical from the wording ('metric/Hilbert stress tensor', 'Noether current', 'improvement term', 'Belinfante') and from whether the tensor is asserted symmetric.

gaps.name: Geometer's positive Laplacian Δ = −∇^a∇_a vs the physicist's ∇²
gaps.what_breaks: In Riemannian geometry, spectral geometry, geometric analysis and heat-kernel work, Δ is defined positive (Δ = dδ + δd, which on functions equals −g^{ab}∇_a∇_b) so that its spectrum is 0 = λ₀ < λ₁ ≤ …; in gr-qc and field theory Δ = ∇^a∇_a with non-positive spectrum. Both are 1/length², so the linter sees nothing, but every equation linear in the Laplacian flips: Green's function normalization, the sign of the heat-kernel exponent and hence of the Seeley–DeWitt/Gilkey coefficients, the Lichnerowicz/Hamiltonian-constraint equation in the conformal method for initial data, the Yamabe operator, and any stability or eigenvalue bound quoted from the math literature into a physics paper.
gaps.magnitude: Sign on the second-derivative term; equivalently the sign of the whole eigenvalue spectrum. Combined with a wrong sign on a curvature term it produces a factor-of-nothing but a qualitatively wrong equation (e.g. an elliptic equation with the wrong-sign potential, changing existence/uniqueness of the solution).
gaps.example: Yamabe/conformal Laplacian: analysts write L_g = −(4(n−1)/(n−2))Δ_g + R_g with Δ_g = div grad (non-positive), while the same operator in the geometers' positive convention is L = (4(n−1)/(n−2))Δ + R with Δ = −div grad. Lichnerowicz equation for maximal, conformally flat initial data: physics form ∇²ψ − (1/8)R̃ψ − (1/8)Ã_abÃ^ab ψ^{−7} = 0 vs the same equation written with the geometers' Δ, Δψ + (1/8)R̃ψ + … = 0. Heat kernel: e^{−tΔ} makes sense only in the positive convention; a physics paper writing e^{−t∇²} means the same operator.
gaps.fingerprint: Look for 'Δ ≥ 0', 'the spectrum 0 = λ₀ < λ₁ ≤ λ₂…', 'Δ = dδ + δd', 'e^{−tΔ}', '−Δu = λu', 'Green's function ΔG = δ' (positive convention) vs '□ = ∇^μ∇_μ', '∇²φ = 4πGρ', 'ΔG = −4πδ' (negative convention). arXiv primary class (math.DG/math.AP vs gr-qc/hep-th) is a strong prior. Cross-check with the Poisson-equation sign if the paper contains a Newtonian limit.

gaps.name: Curvature-normalization family: mean curvature as trace vs average, and scalar vs Gaussian vs sectional curvature
gaps.what_breaks: H, K, R, and the sectional curvature are all L^{-2} and mutually indistinguishable to a dimensional solve, but differ by definite combinatorial factors that vary by community. 'Mean curvature' means the trace of the second fundamental form in general relativity and in mean-curvature-flow analysis, and the average of the principal curvatures in classical surface theory and in membrane/soft-matter physics. 'Curvature of a 2-surface' means the Gaussian curvature K to a geometer and the Ricci scalar R = 2K to a worldsheet or 2d-gravity physicist. Constant-mean-curvature slicing conditions, Gauss–Bonnet prefactors, Helfrich bending energies, and isoperimetric/Alexandrov-type bounds imported across this line all pick up an uncontrolled factor.
gaps.magnitude: Factor n between trace and average (n = 2 for a surface in R³, n = 3 for a spatial slice in 4d spacetime); factor 2 between R and K in two dimensions; factor n(n−1) for the round n-sphere (R = n(n−1)/a² while every sectional curvature is 1/a²). In a Helfrich energy the mismatch is a factor 4 in the bending term and 2 in the spontaneous curvature c₀.
gaps.example: Unit round S² ⊂ R³ (principal curvatures 1, 1): H = κ₁ + κ₂ = 2 (Huisken's mean-curvature-flow convention, and the GR convention H = trK) vs H = (κ₁ + κ₂)/2 = 1 (do Carmo). Gauss–Bonnet, closed 2-manifold: χ = (1/2π)∫K dA (geometry) vs χ = (1/4π)∫√g R d²x (worldsheet Euler term), the two being equal only because R = 2K.
gaps.fingerprint: Read the paper's own Gauss–Bonnet or sphere formula as the calibrator: a 1/4π prefactor on ∫R implies R = 2K bookkeeping, a 1/2π on ∫K implies the geometer's normalization. For H, check whether the traceless part is written σ_ab = A_ab − (H/n)h_ab (average convention) or σ_ab = A_ab − (1/n)H h_ab with H = tr A (trace convention), or look for 'H = h_i{}^i' vs 'H = (1/n)h_i{}^i'. Also check the stated value for a sphere of radius r (n/r vs 1/r) if one appears.

gaps.name: Constants that double as formal grading parameters (α′-, ħ-, G-, 1/c-order counting inside unit systems that set them to 1)
gaps.what_breaks: This is a structural class, not a fork. The tool's system list already contains 'string α′ = 1', 'ℓ_s = 1', natural units with ħ = 1, and geometrized G = c = 1. But in exactly those literatures the same symbol is simultaneously an order-counting grading: an α′ expansion, a loop expansion in ħ, a post-Minkowskian expansion in G, a post-Newtonian expansion in 1/c. Once the generator is set to 1, the tool will either try to restore the constant dimensionally inside a series whose terms are already order-labelled — double counting the powers and reporting a spurious inconsistency — or it will silently absorb the grading and destroy the order bookkeeping. A dimensional check is still possible, but it must be applied order by order with the grading held symbolic, not globally with the generator set to 1.
gaps.magnitude: Not a factor: a category error producing either false 'dimensionally inconsistent' verdicts or an insertion of c^{-2n}/α′^n powers on top of ones already present. In PN work the error is a whole PN order (a relative v²/c² ≈ 10^{-5}–10^{-1}); in the α′ expansion, one power of α′ per erroneous restoration.
gaps.example: Type II effective action written in a paper that also declares α′ = 1: S = (1/2κ²)∫d^{10}x √−g e^{−2Φ}[R + 4(∂Φ)² + (α′/8)(R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} − …) + O(α′²)] — α′ here is dimensionless-by-fiat and simultaneously the expansion grading. Same shape in post-Minkowskian two-body dynamics with G = c = 1: the scattering angle χ/2 = Σ_n χ^{(n)} (G/b)^n, where G is both set to 1 and counted. Same shape with ħ = 1: Γ = S + ħΓ^{(1)} + ħ²Γ^{(2)} + …
gaps.fingerprint: Flag any symbol that appears simultaneously in the declared unit-setting generator list AND as an explicit expansion label — as a superscript/subscript index on a sum, inside an O(·) remainder, or in prose ('α′ corrections', 'nPM order', 'one-loop', 'to 3.5PN'). A declaration 'we set α′ = 1' co-occurring with 'O(α′²)' in the same paper is a hard positive.

gaps.name: Two-component / abstract-index spinor conventions: ε sign and contraction direction
gaps.what_breaks: The tool's fermion handling is limited to γ-matrix riders attached to the signature translation. But the spinor-index calculus carries its own independent convention pair: the sign chosen for ε^{αβ}/ε_{AB}, and the contraction direction (NW–SE, ψχ ≡ ψ^αχ_α, as in Wess–Bagger and Penrose–Rindler, versus the SW–NE contraction ψ_αχ^α). Every Lorentz-invariant fermion bilinear — mass terms, Yukawa terms, Majorana masses, the SUSY algebra, the Weyl spinor Ψ_ABCD components of the Weyl tensor in the 2-spinor formalism — flips sign between them, with no dimensional trace whatsoever.
gaps.magnitude: Exactly −1 per bilinear from the contraction direction: ψχ = ψ^αχ_α = ε^{αβ}ψ_βχ_α = −ψ_αχ^α (direct computation, using ψ^α = ε^{αβ}ψ_β and antisymmetry of ε). A further −1 from flipping the sign convention for ε itself, since each bilinear carries one factor of ε. Composed, the two choices give a Z₂ whose only observable is the product.
gaps.example: Convention A (Wess–Bagger-style): ψ^α = ε^{αβ}ψ_β, ε^{12} = +1, bilinear defined as ψχ ≡ ψ^αχ_α, so a Majorana mass term reads −(m/2)(ψψ + ψ̄ψ̄). Convention B (same ε, SW–NE contraction ψχ ≡ ψ_αχ^α): the identical Lagrangian term is +(m/2)(ψψ + ψ̄ψ̄). In Penrose–Rindler abstract-index form the same choice appears as the see-saw rule ξ^A = ε^{AB}ξ_B, ξ_A = ξ^B ε_{BA}, and reversing it flips the sign of every spinor scalar.
gaps.fingerprint: Grep the conventions appendix for 'ε^{12} =', 'ε_{12} =', 'ε^{αβ}ε_{βγ} =', the phrases 'NW–SE'/'northwest–southeast'/'descending index' or 'see-saw rule', and the paper's own stated identity ψχ = χψ or ψ̄χ̄ = χ̄ψ̄. If absent, read the index staircase off any explicit bilinear in the body: contracted pairs written up-then-down versus down-then-up.

gaps.name: Symplectic / Poisson sign conventions, and the covariant-phase-space charge sign
gaps.what_breaks: Nothing dimensional changes, but the sign of every Hamiltonian flow, bracket, and conserved charge does. The fork is the pair (ordering in the symplectic form: ω = dq∧dp vs dp∧dq) × (definition of the Hamiltonian vector field: ι_{X_H}ω = dH vs −dH), and correspondingly {f,g} = ω(X_f,X_g) vs ω(X_g,X_f). In relativity this propagates into the covariant phase space: whether θ is defined by δL = Eδφ + dθ or with −θ, and whether δH_ξ = ∫_Σ Ω(δφ, £_ξφ) or its negative, which is what fixes the sign of the ADM charges and of δM = (κ/8π)δA + Ω_H δJ. Mathematics and physics sources differ, and papers that mix a math reference's ω with a physics reference's X_H get a time-reversed flow.
gaps.magnitude: Sign of the Hamiltonian flow and of {q,p} (±1); sign of all Noether/Wald charges; equivalently an effective t → −t on the derived dynamics.
gaps.example: With ω = dq∧dp and ι_{X_H}ω = dH one gets X_H = (∂H/∂p)∂_q − (∂H/∂q)∂_p, i.e. q̇ = +∂H/∂p, ṗ = −∂H/∂q (verified by direct contraction). The same rule ι_{X_H}ω = dH applied to ω = dp∧dq gives q̇ = −∂H/∂p, ṗ = +∂H/∂q — the time-reverse. Consistent alternatives are (ω = dp∧dq, ι_{X_H}ω = −dH) and (ω = dq∧dp, ι_{X_H}ω = dH).
gaps.fingerprint: Extract the paper's ω ordering and its X_H/bracket definition and test the pair against Hamilton's equations; or read off the stated {q^i, p_j} = ±δ^i_j. For covariant phase space, check the sign in δL = E δφ + dθ, the definition Ω = ∫δθ, and whether the first law is quoted as δM = (κ/8π)δA or with the opposite sign on the work terms.

gaps.name: Topological-density normalizations: Chern/Pontryagin/Euler prefactors and Hermitian vs anti-Hermitian connections
gaps.what_breaks: The tool's 4π/8π registry covers coupling normalizations, not the 2π-powers that make topological densities integral. Instanton numbers, Chern classes, θ-terms, Euler densities and gravitational anomaly coefficients are dimensionless in every unit system, so the solve is blind, yet their prefactors depend jointly on (i) whether the connection is anti-Hermitian (mathematician: A = −igA_phys^aT^a, F = dA + A∧A) or Hermitian with explicit i and g, (ii) whether the coupling has been absorbed, and (iii) the trace normalization (fundamental with tr T^aT^b = δ^{ab}/2 versus adjoint). Mixing two papers' conventions rescales θ — and therefore any bound derived from it, e.g. the strong-CP θ̄ — by a factor of 2 or 2π-powers.
gaps.magnitude: Factors of 2 and powers of 2π. Equivalent instanton-number normalizations in circulation: N = (1/8π²)∫tr F∧F (anti-Hermitian, F = (1/2)F_μν dx^μ∧dx^ν), N = (1/16π²)∫d⁴x tr F_μν F̃^{μν}, N = (g²/32π²)∫d⁴x F^a_{μν}F̃^{a,μν}. Reading one as another gives factor-2 (or 4π²) errors.
gaps.example: θ-term written as L_θ = (θ g²/32π²) F^a_{μν}F̃^{a,μν} versus L_θ = (θ/16π²) tr F_μν F̃^{μν}: identical physics only under the matched trace/Hermiticity conventions, off by 2 otherwise. Gravitational counterpart: the 4d Euler characteristic χ = (1/32π²)∫d⁴x √g (R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} − 4R_{μν}R^{μν} + R²), whose prefactor no dimensional check can confirm.
gaps.fingerprint: Integrality claims are the anchor and make this lintable: whenever the text asserts a quantity is an integer or a topological invariant ('the instanton number', 'c₁ ∈ H²(M,Z)', 'χ = 2 − 2g', 'winding number'), extract the declared connection convention (does D_μ = ∂_μ + A_μ or ∂_μ − igA_μ?), the trace representation, and the prefactor, and verify the triple against the known normalization. Grep for 'anti-Hermitian', 'tr(T^aT^b) = ', 'F = dA + A∧A' vs 'F_μν = ∂_μA_ν − ∂_νA_μ + ig[A_μ,A_ν]'.

gaps.name: Killing-vector normalization dependence of κ, T_H, Ω_H, and Komar mass
gaps.what_breaks: Surface gravity, Hawking temperature, horizon angular velocity and Komar/quasilocal energies are not properties of the geometry alone: each is defined relative to a normalization of the horizon-generating Killing field. Asymptotic flatness fixes it (ξ·ξ → −1 at infinity), but in AdS, de Sitter, planar black branes, and any non-asymptotically-flat or cosmological setting there is no canonical choice, and different papers normalize at the conformal boundary, at a finite radius, or by a boundary conformal frame. Every variant has identical dimensions, so a converter that rescales numbers between papers silently compares incommensurable quantities. This is structurally like the tool's existing refuse classes (coordinate-absorbed units), but the quantity looks like an ordinary temperature or mass.
gaps.magnitude: An overall multiplicative rescaling with no fixed value: for a static spacetime the Tolman blueshift factor 1/√(−g_tt); for planar AdS black branes a factor of L/r or r_h/L² depending on whether t is normalized so that g_tt → −1 or g_tt → −r²/L².
gaps.example: Schwarzschild: the Hawking temperature measured at infinity is T_∞ = 1/(8πM), while the locally measured Tolman temperature at radius r is T(r) = 1/(8πM√(1 − 2M/r)) — both printed as 'T'. Likewise the Komar mass computed from ξ = ∂_t normalized at infinity versus a rescaled generator ξ' = λξ gives M' = λM with no dimensional symptom.
gaps.fingerprint: Detect non-flat asymptotics (presence of Λ, an AdS radius L, a conformal boundary, a planar/brane horizon, or a cosmological horizon) co-occurring with κ, T_H, Ω_H, or a Komar/quasilocal mass. Then look for an explicit normalization statement ('we normalize ξ so that ξ·ξ = −1 at infinity', 'we choose the boundary metric ds² = −dt² + dx²', 'g_tt → −r²/L²'). If none is present, mark the quantity normalization-ambiguous rather than converting it; also flag any appearance of a redshift factor √(−g_tt) multiplying a temperature or energy elsewhere in the paper as evidence of a local rather than asymptotic normalization.

found.overall: The tool's GR coverage is genuinely strong where relativity meets units — geometrized families, the 8π/16π/32π ladder, little-h, M_Pl variants, bulk sign conventions — so I deliberately did not resubmit anything in that neighborhood. The blind spot is systematic and has a shape: everything the tool knows about GR lives in the bulk, and nothing lives on a hypersurface or a boundary. That is precisely where working relativists get burned (ADM, GHY, Israel junctions, Brown–York, initial-data/conformal method), and it accounts for gaps 1, 2 and part of 4. The second cluster is the math.DG/gr-qc interface: the positive-Laplacian convention and the mean-curvature/scalar-curvature normalizations are invisible to dimensional analysis, cross the literature boundary constantly (CMC slicing, Yamabe/Lichnerowicz, geometric-analysis bounds imported into physics), and are cheap registry/axis work. The third is one structural class I would rank above several registry entries: constants that are simultaneously unit-setting generators and expansion gradings (α′, ħ, G, 1/c). The tool already ships α′ = 1 and ħ = 1 systems, so this is an active internal conflict rather than a hypothetical one, and its symptom is false 'inconsistent' verdicts on perfectly correct string, PM, and PN equations — the worst failure mode for a lint tool, since it trains users to ignore it. Things I considered and rejected as too close to your lists: wedge-product normalization (adjacent to the excluded p!-in-components item), conformal rescaling weights (subsumed by the refused frame-transformation class), the Komar mass/angular-momentum relative factor 2 (a fact people misremember, not a fork between papers), Einstein–Cartan torsion factor 2 (real but narrow), and the Kerr spin-parameter overload a = J/M (length) vs a_* = cJ/GM² (dimensionless) — that last one is common enough to be worth a per-symbol registry row, but it is close in kind to your existing r_g and a₀ entries, so I left it here rather than in the list.

verdict.lens: Mathematical relativity / differential geometry: 3+1 and hypersurface geometry (ADM, GHY, Israel, Brown–York, conformal method), variational and boundary bookkeeping, curvature normalizations shared with math.DG, spinor-bundle and symplectic conventions, and unit-setting constants doubling as expansion gradings.

verdicts.gap: Extrinsic-curvature sign × normal orientation (the whole hypersurface axis)
verdicts.notes: Recomputed and source-checked. Attribution is right: MTW (K_ij = −n_{i;j}), Gourgoulhon (3+1 notes, K = γ^ij K_ij = −3H, minus chosen to match the NR/Baumgarte–Shapiro community), Alcubierre = minus; Wald, Poisson's Toolkit, and also Carroll = plus. FLRW check: n = ∂_t, K = ∇_a n^a = 3H with the plus convention, −3H with the minus. Sphere check: div(r̂) = 2/r in flat R³, so K = +2/r (Wald, outward normal) vs −2/r. Israel sign as quoted matches the Toolkit, S_ab = −(1/8π)([K_ab] − [K]h_ab). The two-declaration structure (K sign × normal orientation, only the product observable) is genuine and is the reason the 'declare one, infer the other' failure survives. Not in the round-2 sign axis, which is entirely bulk (Riemann sign, Ricci contraction, ε0123, D_μ charge, Fourier); not in the round-3 exclusions. Quadratic-invariance remark is correct (K_abK^ab − K² and the ADM kinetic term are parity-even). new_axis / v1 is the right slot — unlike a single sign flag this is a product of two declarations propagating into a fixed list of derived objects (GHY, π^ij, S_ab, Brown–York ε), and 'declares neither ⇒ under-determined, do not guess' is the correct default given the tool's existing residual-rank-honesty posture.

verdicts.gap: Stress tensor from metric variation: sign, index position of the varied metric, and Hilbert-vs-canonical kind
verdicts.notes: Variation recomputed independently. With δ√−g = −(1/2)√−g g_μν δg^{μν} and L_m = −(1/2)g^{μν}∂_μφ∂_νφ − V: δS_m/δg^{μν} = √−g[−(1/2)∂_μφ∂_νφ − (1/2)g_μν L_m], so T_μν = −(2/√−g)δS_m/δg^{μν} = ∂_μφ∂_νφ + g_μν L_m = ∂_μφ∂_νφ − g_μν[(1/2)(∂φ)² + V]. Mostly-plus, φ = φ(t): (∂φ)² = −φ̇², T_00 = φ̇² + (−(1/2)φ̇² + V) = (1/2)φ̇² + V > 0. Confirms the claimed positivity check and the equivalence T_μν = −(2/√−g)δS_m/δg^{μν} = +(2/√−g)δS^{μν}-form via δg^{μν} = −g^{μα}g^{νβ}δg_{αβ}. The three-way interlock (variation index position × explicit sign × sign of L_m in the action) is real, dimensionally silent, and absent from both lists. Two trims for the spec, not the verdict: (i) the Hilbert / canonical-Noether / Belinfante leg is not a sign fork at all but a quantity-kind distinction, and as such it is the same schema feature as excluded item (5) (quantity-kind tags, Gy vs Sv, χ_v/χ_mol/χ_g) — implement it as a tag on that existing feature rather than as part of the new sign axis; (ii) the positivity sanity check only bites for matter satisfying WEC, so it must be gated off for phantom/ghost/negative-tension-brane papers where ρ < 0 is intentional.

verdicts.gap: Geometer's positive Laplacian Δ = −∇^a∇_a vs the physicist's ∇²
verdicts.notes: Physics is right and the gap is real. Δ = dδ + δd on functions equals −g^{ab}∇_a∇_b, spectrum 0 = λ₀ < λ₁ ≤ …; e^{−tΔ} only makes sense in the positive convention; the conformal/Yamabe operator is L_g = −[4(n−1)/(n−2)]Δ_g + R_g with the analysts' non-positive Δ and flips its relative sign under the geometers'. Lichnerowicz example is directionally correct (the physics form is ∇̃²ψ − (1/8)R̃ψ − (1/8)Ã_abÃ^ab ψ^{−7} + (1/12)K²ψ⁵ = …, and the geometers' Δ flips the second-derivative term against the rest). Not in coverage, not in exclusions. But the treatment is mis-slotted: this is a single binary flag on one operator with no product structure and no per-symbol table — exactly parallel to 'Fourier sign', which already lives as an entry on the round-2 sign-convention axis. It belongs there as one more entry (with the Green's-function normalization ΔG = δ vs ∇²G = −4πδ as its calibrator), not as a standalone new axis. Keep v1; downgrade new_axis → entry on the existing sign axis.

verdicts.gap: Curvature-normalization family: mean curvature as trace vs average, and scalar vs Gaussian vs sectional curvature
verdicts.notes: All arithmetic checks out. Unit round S² ⊂ R³ (κ₁ = κ₂ = 1): H = 2 (trace; Huisken's MCF and GR H = tr K) vs H = 1 (do Carmo average) — factor n = 2, and n = 3 for a spatial slice in 4d. Gauss–Bonnet: χ = (1/2π)∫K dA vs χ = (1/4π)∫√g R d²x, consistent only because R = 2K in two dimensions. Round n-sphere of radius a: sectional curvature 1/a² for every 2-plane, Ricci scalar R = n(n−1)/a², so the trace factor is n(n−1) as claimed. Helfrich: with H_trace = 2H_avg, (κ/2)∫(2H_avg − c₀)² = (κ/2)∫(H_trace − c₀)², so importing the wrong H gives factor 4 in the bending term at c₀ = 0 and factor 2 in c₀ — as stated. Distinct from excluded item (4) (p! in form components, Levi-Civita symbol vs density, Hodge sign), which is forms bookkeeping, not curvature trace normalization. registry_entry / v1 is right: these are fixed rational factors keyed to a symbol name, exactly the shape of the existing 21-fork registry, and the paper's own Gauss–Bonnet prefactor or sphere value is a clean in-document calibrator.

verdicts.gap: Constants that double as formal grading parameters (α′-, ħ-, G-, 1/c-order counting inside unit systems that set them to 1)
verdicts.notes: The structural class is real but the failure analysis is too broad, and the flagship example is dimensionally wrong. (a) The PM example as written is not the PM expansion: G/b is not dimensionless in any system (in G = c = 1 it is 1/length), so χ = Σ χ^(n)(G/b)^n cannot be the actual grading — the real parameter is GM/(bc²) (or Gm/(bv²)), which is dimensionless and therefore not something the tool would try to restore at all. (b) For PN and α′ series the generic behaviour is the opposite of what is claimed: per-term dimensional restoration in c = 1 or α′ = 1 units recovers exactly the powers c^{−2n}/α′^n that define the order, i.e. the solve reconstructs the grading rather than double-counting it. If a term already carries its explicit α′ power the residual exponent solves to zero; there is no spurious 'inconsistent' verdict. Corrected claim, narrower and still worth shipping: the real failure has two heads — (i) mixed notation, where a paper sets α′ = 1 but retains explicit α′ labels on only some terms (or only inside O(·)), so the same symbol is dimensionful in one term and a bare counter in another; and (ii) loop counting in ħ, which is genuinely non-dimensional: in Γ = S + ħΓ^(1) + ħ²Γ^(2) + … the loop order is not recoverable from dimensions because the dimension of each Γ^(L) is not independently fixed, so ħ-as-counter must be declared, never restored. The magnitude line should drop 'a whole PN order' as the headline; the honest statement is 'one power of the grading symbol on terms written in mixed notation, and an unrecoverable loop index for ħ'. Treatment: schema_feature is right, but implement it as a per-symbol non-restorable flag on the existing residue machinery (residues Re, Ra, J/t are already never restored) rather than as new solve logic, and demote v1 → v2 given the narrowed scope.

verdicts.gap: Two-component / abstract-index spinor conventions: ε sign and contraction direction
verdicts.notes: The Z₂ pair is real and genuinely uncovered — the round-2 fermion handling is γ-matrix riders attached to signature, which says nothing about the undotted-index staircase — and the identity is right: ψ^αχ_α = ε^{αβ}ψ_βχ_α while ψ_αχ^α = ε^{αβ}ψ_αχ_β = −ε^{αβ}ψ_βχ_α (relabel + antisymmetry), so ψχ = −ψ_αχ^α. What is overstated is 'every Lorentz-invariant fermion bilinear flips'. The flip is a parity count in ε insertions, so it hits only odd-ε bilinears: the scalar ψχ, ψ̄χ̄ mass, Yukawa and Majorana terms. Even-ε objects are invariant — the vector bilinear ψσ^μχ̄ = ψ^ασ^μ_{αα̇}χ̄^{α̇} carries two ε's, the SUSY anticommutator {Q,Q̄} = 2σ^μP_μ likewise, and the Weyl-tensor spinor components Ψ_0…Ψ_4 = Ψ_ABCD o…ι carry four, so all of these are untouched. Drop the Weyl-tensor and SUSY-algebra items from the example list and restate the magnitude as 'exactly −1 per ε insertion; net −1 on odd-ε (scalar) bilinears, +1 on even-ε (vector) ones'. new_axis / v2 stands, though it could equally ride the existing sign axis next to the γ-riders since only the product ε-sign × contraction-direction is observable.

verdicts.gap: Symplectic / Poisson sign conventions, and the covariant-phase-space charge sign
verdicts.notes: Contraction recomputed: for X = a∂_q + b∂_p, ι_X(dq∧dp) = a dp − b dq; setting this equal to dH = (∂_qH)dq + (∂_pH)dp gives a = ∂H/∂p and b = −∂H/∂q, i.e. q̇ = +∂H/∂p, ṗ = −∂H/∂q — the claimed result, and its exact time-reverse under ω = dp∧dq with the same ι_{X_H}ω = dH rule. The math/physics split is real (Arnold-style ω = dp∧dq vs the physicists' dq∧dp; ω(X_H, ·) = dH vs = −dH), it is dimensionally silent, and neither the coverage list nor the exclusions touch Hamiltonian/Poisson structure. One caveat for the spec: the covariant-phase-space leg is weaker than the mechanics leg. Intermediate objects (θ in δL = Eδφ + dθ, Ω = ∫δθ, δH_ξ) genuinely differ in sign between references, but the final first law δM = (κ/8π)δA + Ω_HδJ is not printed with the opposite overall sign, because M is pinned to the ADM mass by physical normalization — so the first law is a calibrator, not a fork. Anchor detection on {q^i, p_j} = ±δ^i_j and on the θ/Ω definitions, not on the first law. new_axis / v2 stands.

verdicts.gap: Topological-density normalizations: Chern/Pontryagin/Euler prefactors and Hermitian vs anti-Hermitian connections
verdicts.notes: Normalizations check out and are mutually consistent under matched conventions: with fundamental-rep trace tr(T^aT^b) = δ^{ab}/2, (1/16π²)∫d⁴x tr F_μν F̃^{μν} = (1/32π²)∫d⁴x F^a_{μν}F̃^{a,μν}, matching the standard strong-CP θ-term L_θ = (θg²/32π²)F^aF̃^a for a g-absorbed field, and the anti-Hermitian form N = (1/8π²)∫tr F∧F with F = (1/2)F_μν dx^μ∧dx^ν. The 4d Euler density prefactor 1/32π² on (R_{μνρσ}² − 4R_{μν}² + R²) is correct. Two trims. (i) Leg (ii) of the triple — 'whether the coupling has been absorbed' — is already the registry's 'g-absorbed gauge field L = −F²/4g²' row; the new content is legs (i) Hermitian vs anti-Hermitian and (iii) trace representation, so write it as an extension of that existing row rather than an independent entry. (ii) The 'powers of 2π' half of the magnitude is largely self-detecting: θ ≡ θ + 2π periodicity and integrality of the instanton number are internal anchors that a 2π-power error violates immediately, which is exactly what the proposed fingerprint exploits. The live residual magnitude is the factor 2 (trace normalization / Hermiticity) and the overall sign, and for adjoint-vs-fundamental it is 2N for SU(N), not 2. registry_entry / v2 and confidence 'likely' are both appropriate.

verdicts.gap: Killing-vector normalization dependence of κ, T_H, Ω_H, and Komar mass
verdicts.notes: Core is real: κ, T_H, Ω_H and Komar mass are defined relative to a normalization of the horizon-generating Killing field, ξ → λξ rescales κ and M by λ with no dimensional trace, and in asymptotically AdS, de Sitter, planar-brane and cosmological settings there is no canonical fix. But the flagship example is a category slip. Schwarzschild T_∞ = κ/2π = 1/(8πM) (κ = 1/4M — recomputed) and the Tolman T(r) = T_∞/√(1 − 2M/r) are not two conventions for one quantity; they are two physically distinct measurements (temperature at infinity vs at a static observer at radius r), and asymptotic flatness fixes ξ·ξ → −1 uniquely, so the fork does not exist in the asymptotically flat case at all. Since asymptotically flat black-hole papers are the bulk of the κ/T_H/Komar literature, the prevalence is substantially narrower than stated. Corrected claim: the ambiguity is confined to non-asymptotically-flat horizons — planar AdS branes (where the fork is the boundary-metric choice, t normalized against g_tt → −r²/L² vs a stripped boundary metric −dt² + dx², giving T = d·r_h/4πL² up to the conformal factor, not the loosely quoted 'L/r'), de Sitter/cosmological horizons, and Λ ≠ 0 quasilocal masses. Treatment is also mis-slotted as stated: refuse_class over-refuses, since a paper that declares its boundary normalization yields a perfectly convertible quantity. Implement as a conditional normalization-ambiguous tag (refuse only when no normalization statement is found), which is what the claim's own fingerprint actually describes. v2 is right.

verdict.overall: Strong round from this lens. The framing claim — that the tool's GR knowledge is all bulk and none of it lives on a hypersurface or boundary — is accurate and is not covered anywhere in the coverage summary or the round-3 exclusions. Four gaps survive clean: extrinsic-curvature sign × normal orientation (1), the stress-tensor variation interlock (2), the mean-curvature/scalar-curvature normalization family (4), and the symplectic/Poisson sign pair (7). All four were recomputed and hold; gap 1's source attributions (MTW/Gourgoulhon/Alcubierre minus, Wald/Poisson/Carroll plus, K = ∓3H in FLRW, Israel S_ab = −(1/8π)([K_ab] − [K]h_ab)) were independently confirmed, as were gap 2's scalar-field variation (T_00 = ½φ̇² + V), gap 4's sphere and Gauss–Bonnet arithmetic, and gap 7's ι_{X_H}ω contraction. Three real-but-trimmed. Gap 6 (spinor ε and contraction direction) is genuinely uncovered — the round-2 γ-riders do not reach the index staircase — but the flip is a parity count in ε insertions, so it hits scalar mass/Yukawa/Majorana bilinears and NOT the vector bilinear, the SUSY anticommutator, or the Weyl-tensor components; those three examples should come out. Gap 9's Killing-normalization claim is real only off asymptotic flatness, and its Schwarzschild Tolman example is two distinct physical quantities rather than a convention fork; it also wants a conditional tag, not a refuse class. Gap 8 is confirmed with the coupling-absorption leg folded into the existing g-absorbed-field registry row and the 2π-power magnitude trimmed, since integrality and θ-periodicity make those errors self-detecting. Two corrections of substance. Gap 5, which the critic ranked highest, is the weakest: its PM example is dimensionally incoherent (G/b is not the expansion parameter; GM/bc² is), and for PN and α′ series per-term dimensional restoration reconstructs the grading rather than double-counting it, so the advertised 'false inconsistent verdicts on correct string/PM/PN equations' is not the generic behaviour. What survives is narrower and still worth having: mixed notation where a grading symbol is dimensionful in some terms and a bare counter in others, and ħ-as-loop-counter, which is genuinely unrecoverable dimensionally. That belongs on the existing never-restore residue machinery at v2, not as v1 solve logic. Gap 3 is a mis-slot, not a miss: the geometers' positive Laplacian is a single binary flag with an in-document calibrator, structurally identical to the already-shipped 'Fourier sign', so it should be one more entry on the round-2 sign axis rather than a fourth new axis. Net: 4 confirmed, 1 wrong_treatment, 3 overstated, 1 partially duplicative but confirmed; nothing not_real and nothing a straight duplicate. The critic's self-policing at the end (rejecting wedge normalization, conformal weights, the Komar factor 2, Einstein–Cartan torsion) is sound, and the Kerr a vs a_* item they held back is correctly judged too close to the existing r_g row.
